source.title: Recent developments and open problems in the theory of permanents

accepted.question_text: For an n x n doubly stochastic matrix A with all diagonal entries equal to 0, where doubly stochastic means that A has nonnegative entries and every row and column sums to 1, and where per(A) is the permanent of A, is per(A) minimized uniquely by the matrix whose diagonal entries are 0 and whose off-diagonal entries are 1/(n-1)?
Let D_n be the set of n-tuples (A_1,...,A_n) of n x n positive semidefinite matrices such that trace(A_i)=1 for every i and A_1+...+A_n=I. Which elements of D_n are extreme points of this convex set?

Can one give a unifying explanation for the similarities between matrix positivity as a positive-semidefinite operator condition, meaning a Hermitian matrix A with x*Ax >= 0 for every vector x, and entrywise positivity or nonnegativity, especially for permanent inequalities and related matrix properties?

Let A=(a_ij) be an n x n positive semidefinite matrix. Fix an ordering of the permutation group S_n and define the Schur power pi(A) to be the n! x n! matrix indexed by permutations sigma and tau in S_n, with (sigma,tau)-entry equal to the product over i=1,...,n of a_{sigma(i),tau(i)}. Is per(A) the largest eigenvalue of pi(A)?

Let A=(a_ij) be an n x n positive semidefinite matrix, let G be a subgroup of the permutation group S_n, and let chi be a complex character on G. Does the permanent dominate the corresponding immanant, in the sense that per(A) >= sum over sigma in G of chi(sigma) times the product over i=1,...,n of a_{i,sigma(i)}?

For n x n positive semidefinite matrices A=(a_ij) and B=(b_ij), let A o B denote their Schur product, meaning the entrywise product (a_ij b_ij). Does the permanent inequality per(A o B) <= per(A) b_11 b_22 ... b_nn always hold?
accepted.context_brief: Permanent analogue of Oppenheim-type Schur product inequality

accepted.question_text: Let A=(a_ij) be an n x n positive semidefinite matrix, and let A(i,j) be the submatrix obtained by deleting row i and column j of A. Is per(A) the largest eigenvalue of the n x n matrix whose (i,j)-entry is a_ij per(A(i,j))?

Let A be an n x n positive semidefinite matrix and let 1 <= k <= n-1. Let G_{k,n} be the set of strictly increasing functions from {1,...,k} to {1,...,n}. For alpha,beta in G_{k,n}, let A[alpha,beta] be the k x k submatrix of A with rows indexed by alpha and columns indexed by beta, and let A(alpha,beta) be the complementary (n-k) x (n-k) submatrix. Define C_k(A) to be the matrix indexed by G_{k,n} with entry per(A(alpha,beta)) per(A[alpha,beta]) at (alpha,beta). Is per(A) the largest eigenvalue of C_k(A) for every k=1,...,n-1?

For an n x n positive semidefinite matrix A=(a_ij) and real q, define the q-permanent per_q(A) as the sum over permutations sigma in S_n of q raised to the inversion number of sigma, multiplied by the product over i=1,...,n of a_{i,sigma(i)}. Is per_q(A), as a function of q, monotonically increasing on the interval [-1,1]?

For an n x n positive semidefinite matrix A=(a_ij) and real alpha, define det_alpha(A) as the sum over permutations sigma in S_n of alpha raised to n minus the number of cycles of sigma, multiplied by the product over i=1,...,n of a_{i,sigma(i)}. If 0 <= alpha <= 2, must det_alpha(A) be nonnegative?

Fix positive vectors c,b_1,b_2,... in R^n. For a positive vector x in R^n and 1 <= r <= n, define S_{r,n}(x) as per[x repeated r times, b_1,...,b_{n-r}] divided by per[x repeated r-1 times, b_1,...,b_{n-r}, c], where per[...] is the permanent of the matrix whose displayed vectors are its columns. For any positive vectors x and y, does S_{r,n}(x+y) >= S_{r,n}(x)+S_{r,n}(y) hold?
accepted.context_brief: Permanent generalization of symmetric function mean inequality

trace.notes: Normalized the input as the zbMATH resolver URL https://zbmath.org/5575758. Direct shell fetch of the landing page returned a Cloudflare challenge, so the zbMATH REST API was used only as resolver metadata and identified Zbl 1175.15007: R. B. Bapat, 'Recent developments and open problems in the theory of permanents', The Mathematics Student 76, no. 1-4, pages 55-69, 2007.

Exact-title recovery found a readable PDF of the same work at CiteseerX and an official Indian Mathematical Society issue PDF. Local curl could not resolve the PDF hosts, but the web/PDF reader exposed the full Bapat paper text with visible title and page text, so extraction used the CiteseerX PDF as the readable primary artifact.

Mapped the PDF into sections: 1 Introduction; 2 Matrices of zeros and ones; 3 Nonnegative matrices; 4 Mixed discriminants; 5 Positive definite matrices; 6 A q-analogue of the permanent; 7 Computation of the permanent; 8 Symmetric function means and permanents. Likely open-problem regions occur on pages 6-15, especially the formal Conjectures 1-9 and the explicit extreme-point problem for D_n.
The introduction supplies the definition of permanent and scope but no standalone open-problem candidate.
The section on 0-1 matrices discusses solved background results and no current standalone open-problem candidate was accepted from this section.
Extracted q_001 from the folklore conjecture on minimizing permanents over zero-diagonal doubly stochastic matrices.

Extracted q_002 from the explicit problem of characterizing extreme points of D_n. A nearby mixed-discriminant minimization conjecture was not accepted because the same source says it had already been proved by Gurvits.

Extracted q_003 through q_008: the Taussy unification problem, Soules' Schur-power conjecture, permanental dominance, the Schur-product permanent inequality, the permanental cofactor eigenvalue conjecture, and Pate's C_k(A) generalization.
Extracted q_009 and q_010 from the q-permanent monotonicity conjecture and the alpha-determinant nonnegativity conjecture.
The computation section describes complexity and approximation background but does not state a standalone open problem in the source text.
Extracted q_011 from the conjectured superadditivity inequality for S_{r,n}, a permanent generalization of symmetric function means.
Expanded the zero-diagonal doubly stochastic matrix setting and the permanent-minimizer matrix into a standalone question.
Inlined the definition of D_n and rewrote the extreme-point problem as a direct characterization question.
Inlined the two notions of positivity needed for the Taussy unification problem.
Inlined the definition of the Schur power pi(A) and the eigenvalue claim.
Expanded the permanental dominance conjecture with the subgroup, character, and immanant expression.
Expanded the Schur product notation and the permanent inequality.
Expanded the deleted-row-and-column submatrix notation A(i,j).
Expanded G_{k,n}, the submatrix notation, and the construction of C_k(A).
Expanded the q-permanent definition using inversion number and the monotonicity interval.
Expanded the alpha-determinant definition using the number of cycles of a permutation.
Expanded the S_{r,n} quotient and the role of the displayed vectors in the permanent.
